newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO links municipal polls to Israeli withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: PLO links municipal polls to Israeli withdrawal.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority will delay the first municipal elections under PLO rule until Israel completes troop withdrawals from West Bank rural areas, a PLO official said on Sunday.

"We are linking the municipal elections to redeployment of Israeli troops from the rest of the West Bank. Since Israel did not complete withdrawal yet, we have decided to postpone the local elections," said Palestinian Authority Minister of Local Government Saeb Erekat.
The elections were set for this August after an earlier delay from October 1996, a month after Israel was due to have begun evacuating from West Bank rural areas under a 1995 peace deal with the PLO.
Erekat told Reuters that 90 percent of Palestinian municipalities were in areas still under Israeli security control. Most of the areas fall under Palestinian civil jurisdiction.

"Unfortunately since Israel has frozen its withdrawal, we can't take the risk of holding elections under occupation and our local elections are the first in Palestinian history under Palestinian rule," Erekat said.
Israel has handed over to the PLO most of the Gaza Strip, seven West Bank cities and part of an eighth under 1993 and 1995 peace deals.

It also redeployed in April from nine percent of the West Bank in a move which angered Palestinians, who were expecting to receive three times that amount in the first of three Israeli pullbacks from rural areas slated to end in mid-1998.
Erekat said 374 municipalities in the West Bank and Gaza Strip had already started preparations for the elections.
PLO-Israeli peace moves have been suspended since March when Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Erekat said on Saturday he had appointed Hanna Nasser mayor of Bethlehem after the resignation of Elias Freij last month.
"I have also appointed a 24-member committee, headed by Hanna Nasser to serve Bethlehem municipality until municipal elections are held," he said.
Nasser was Freij's deputy. Freij, mayor since 1972 and Tourism Minister in the Palestinian Authority, resigned from public life after 51 years of service for health reasons.
